title: Azure Monitor metrics and log settings
learningObjective: Interpret metrics in Metrics explorer and configure the right collection (activity log, diagnostic settings, Azure Monitor Agent with data collection rules) and destinations.

prerequisites.text: Basic familiarity with VMs and storage accounts

foundation: Azure Monitor collects two main kinds of data: metrics (numbers over time, such as CPU %) and logs (records of events with many fields).
Platform metrics are collected automatically for most resources. Logs from inside resources need configuration.
A chart only shows what its aggregation and time grain reveal: a 1-hour average can hide a 3-minute spike.
engineer: Metrics: platform metrics every minute, kept 93 days; Metrics explorer chooses scope, metric, aggregation (Average, Min, Max, Sum, Count), time range and granularity; split or filter by dimensions (for example per disk LUN or per API name). Pin charts to dashboards or workbooks.
Activity log: subscription-level control-plane events (create, delete, role changes, service health), kept 90 days. Export with a diagnostic setting for longer retention or KQL.

Resource logs (data-plane: Key Vault access, storage reads, NSG events) are not collected until you create a diagnostic setting choosing categories and destinations: Log Analytics workspace (query/alert), Storage account (archive), Event Hubs (stream to SIEM), partner solutions. Up to 5 diagnostic settings per resource.

Guest OS data (performance counters, Windows events, Syslog, text logs) needs the Azure Monitor Agent plus a data collection rule (DCR) that says what to collect and where to send it. The legacy Log Analytics agent is retired.
Log Analytics workspace settings: region, access control mode (resource-context or workspace), table plans and retention (interactive retention plus long-term retention up to 12 years), daily cap.

example.title: A slow website
body: The 1-hour average CPU chart looks fine, but switching to Maximum at 1-minute granularity reveals 97% spikes every evening during backups.
To investigate requests, the team adds a diagnostic setting on the App Service sending HTTP logs to Log Analytics.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with VMs to monitor or protect
permissions: Monitoring Contributor (alerts, diagnostic settings) or Backup Contributor (vaults, policies)
limits: See Azure Monitor / Azure Backup service limits
portal: Monitor > Metrics: select scope, metric, aggregation; set time range and granularity; Apply splitting.
Resource > Diagnostic settings > + Add: choose categories and destinations.
Monitor > Data collection rules > Create: choose VMs (installs AMA), data sources and the workspace.
Monitor > Activity log: filter and export.
configuration.cli:
az monitor metrics list --resource $VM_ID --metric "Percentage CPU" --aggregation Maximum --interval PT1M
az monitor log-analytics workspace create -g rg-mon -n law-ops --retention-time 90
az monitor diagnostic-settings create -n to-law --resource $KV_ID --workspace law-ops --logs '[{"categoryGroup":"allLogs","enabled":true}]' --metrics '[{"category":"AllMetrics","enabled":true}]'
az monitor data-collection rule create -g rg-mon -n dcr-windows --location eastus --rule-file dcr.json
az monitor activity-log list --offset 1d --query "[?operationName.value=='Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions/resourceGroups/delete']"
configuration.powershell:
Get-AzMetric -ResourceId $vmId -MetricName 'Percentage CPU' -AggregationType Maximum -TimeGrain 00:01:00
New-AzOperationalInsightsWorkspace -ResourceGroupName rg-mon -Name law-ops -Location eastus -Sku PerGB2018
$log = New-AzDiagnosticSettingLogSettingsObject -CategoryGroup allLogs -Enabled $true
New-AzDiagnosticSetting -Name to-law -ResourceId $kvId -WorkspaceId $lawId -Log $log
Get-AzActivityLog -StartTime (Get-Date).AddDays(-1)

troubleshooting.symptom: Log Analytics has no Key Vault logs.
troubleshooting.fix: Create one with the AuditEvent/allLogs category.

troubleshooting.symptom: Perf table is empty for a VM.
troubleshooting.cause: No Azure Monitor Agent or DCR.

troubleshooting.symptom: Can't see who deleted a resource 4 months ago.
troubleshooting.fix: Export the activity log to a workspace or storage.

comparisons.difference: Metrics, logs and alarms; CloudTrail is the activity log equivalent.
Application performance monitoring (requests, dependencies, traces) built on Azure Monitor.

misconceptions.reality: Only platform metrics and the activity log; resource and guest logs need configuration.

misconceptions.myth: The average shows the worst case.

architectureDecisions: Send logs to one central workspace per environment unless data residency or access requires more.
Use Azure Policy to deploy diagnostic settings and DCRs at scale.
Set retention and table plans to control cost.

walkthrough.subtitle: Know what Azure collects for you automatically, and what you must switch on.
learn: Guest OS data with Azure Monitor Agent

steps.label: What happened?
steps.title: The app was slow last night. Why?
body: To answer, you need data that was already being collected. Some of it Azure keeps automatically; some you must turn on beforehand.

steps.label: Metrics
steps.title: Metrics are collected automatically
body: Every resource sends platform metrics (CPU, transactions, latency) every minute, kept for 93 days, free. View them in Metrics explorer.
Pick the aggregation carefully: Avg, Min, Max, Sum or Count, over a time granularity such as 1 minute or 1 hour. Split or filter by dimensions, for example by API name.

callout.text: A 1-hour average hides a 5-minute spike. Use Max and a small granularity to find spikes.

steps.label: Logs
steps.title: Two kinds of logs
body: The activity log records control-plane operations on the subscription: who created, changed or deleted what. Kept 90 days, free.
Resource logs record what happens inside a resource (for example every blob read). They are not collected until you create a diagnostic setting.

steps.label: Destinations
steps.title: Where a diagnostic setting sends data
body: Send to a Log Analytics workspace (to query and alert), a storage account (cheap archive) or Event Hubs (to stream to other tools), or a partner solution. One resource can have several diagnostic settings.

steps.label: Guest OS
steps.title: Inside the VM: Azure Monitor Agent
body: Platform metrics only see the VM from outside. For memory, disk space, Windows events or Syslog, install the Azure Monitor Agent and create a data collection rule (DCR) that says what to collect and where to send it. The old Log Analytics agent is retired.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Metrics and logs
body: Metrics and activity log are free and automatic; the rest you switch on.
recap: Choose aggregation and granularity with care
Activity log = who did what (90 days)
Resource logs need a diagnostic setting
Guest OS data: Azure Monitor Agent + DCR

handsOn.title: Read metrics and send storage logs to Log Analytics
handsOn.cost: Cents. A small Log Analytics workspace with a few log entries costs almost nothing.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.
A storage account in rg-az104-lab with a container and one uploaded file.

steps.do: Open the storage account > Monitoring > Metrics. Metric: Transactions, aggregation: Sum. Time range: last hour.
Select 'Apply splitting' and split by API name.
steps.see: Separate lines for operations such as GetBlob or ListBlobs.

steps.do: Search 'Log Analytics workspaces' > + Create. Group rg-az104-lab, name law-lab, region your region. Create.

Open the storage account > Monitoring > Diagnostic settings > blob > + Add diagnostic setting. Name diag-blob, tick StorageRead, StorageWrite, StorageDelete and Transaction, destination: law-lab. Save.
steps.see: diag-blob listed for the blob service.

steps.do: Upload and download a couple of files in the container to create activity.
Search 'Activity log'. Filter Resource group: rg-az104-lab.
steps.see: Entries such as 'Create or Update Diagnostic Setting' with who did it and when.

steps.do: After 5–10 minutes open law-lab > Logs and run: StorageBlobLogs | take 20
steps.see: Rows for your blob operations, with caller IP and status.

steps.do: Open the storage account > Monitoring > Diagnostic settings again and read the 'Storage account' level option (account metrics only).

check: StorageBlobLogs returns your operations in law-lab.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
